inputs.text: This is exactly how global crises deepen inequality: households and workers are made to absorb higher costs, while people with the most wealth and power are better placed to ride them out. Cutting fuel duties may offer temporary relief, but if the lost revenue is later recovered through weaker public services or other burdens on ordinary people, that is not a fair solution. India’s dependence on imported crude leaves people vulnerable to shocks they did not cause. We need a just, resilient energy transition that protects workers and low-income households instead of repeatedly asking them to pay the price.
